clue.text: Party of excavators embarrassed after losing axes

indicators.note: to lose something is to be left without it, so the named letters are taken out of the longer word
someone embarrassed is flustered and thrown into disorder, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: these four letters are removed one each from the longer word

explanation.surface: A gang of diggers, red-faced after mislaying their axes, holds a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A, X, E and S from EXCAVATORS to leave C, V, A, T, O, R, then rearrange them as CAVORT. 'Party' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To cavort is to leap about in high spirits, which is what partying people do.

clue.text: Baked item: first complaint to brawny men

indicators.note: first tells us which piece comes at the front of the answer, ahead of the other one

blocks.note: a beef is slang for a grievance

explanation.surface: A complaint about a baked item is being sent to some burly men.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefcake is slang for muscular men shown off for their physique, especially in photographs.

clue.text: Addresses with sailor's poem enclosed

indicators.note: something enclosed is held inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor; the 's adds S
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: Postal addresses arrive with a sailor's verse tucked inside the envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the standard crossword sailor; 'Addresses' is a noun meaning homes, not speeches or the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An abode is a dwelling place, and your address is where you live, so plural homes fit.

clue.text: Nest lad disturbed and left at an angle

indicators.note: a disturbed thing has been knocked out of its order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy upsets a bird's nest and leaves it lying crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Something slanted has been placed on a slope, tilted rather than set straight or level.

clue.text: Harass a wild animal

blocks.note: first meaning: to pester someone persistently
second meaning: a burrowing black-and-white mammal

explanation.surface: Someone is tormenting a creature of the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one action on an animal, but the verb and the animal are two separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to nag persistently; the noun is a nocturnal mammal with a striped face that digs setts.

clue.text: Wing around pine construction in Canadian city

indicators.note: a construction is something built up from parts, so the letters of the tree are reassembled
to be around something is to surround it, so one word wraps the other

explanation.surface: An extension wing is being built around pine timber in a city in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the tree's letters are rearranged; the wing stays in order and opens up after its third letter to hold them.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnipeg is the capital of the province of Manitoba in central Canada.

clue.text: Organise a dance and enjoy a good time

blocks.note: first meaning, taken literally: to hold a formal dancing party
second meaning: the idiom for having great fun

explanation.surface: Throw a dance party and have fun doing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, holding a ball means staging a dance; idiomatically the phrase means having tremendous fun.

clue.text: Byword for graduate, team's top man

indicators.note: the top of a word written downwards is its first letter, so only the opening one is kept

blocks.note: MA is a Master of Arts
a cricket or football team is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A university graduate's name has become a byword as the team's leading figure.
explanation.walkthrough: XI for a team is a crossword staple: eleven players in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: A maxim is a short saying of general truth, and a byword can be such a proverb.

clue.text: Without a doubt, privately reveal name and model

blocks.note: to confide is to tell something in secret
N is the abbreviation for name
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: Someone certain of themselves quietly discloses a name and the model involved.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ford Model T lets 'model' stand for T.
explanation.definitionFit: Being confident means feeling sure, holding no doubt at all about something.

clue.text: Single male representative

explanation.surface: An unmarried man acts as someone's representative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' looks like it means unmarried; it simply gives A, one.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent acts on behalf of another person, such as a sports star or a firm.

clue.text: Area where last character's alone, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so a letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A place where the final person is left largely isolated.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'mostly' drops the first letter rather than the usual last one.
explanation.definitionFit: A zone is a region or district set apart for some purpose, such as a war zone.

clue.text: Wanders with good person, artist's unknown son

blocks.note: algebra's unknowns are x, y and z
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A drifter travels with a kindly person, and the painter's son is a stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, member of the Royal Academy of Arts, is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to roam off the proper path, so it matches the verb for roving about aimlessly.

clue.text: English go on excursions for self-aggrandisement

definitions.note: the answer is a plural noun; the definition is a mass noun

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: English people head off on outings to make themselves feel important.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego trips are acts done to boost one's own importance or vanity, which is self-aggrandisement.

clue.text: Heads up to see the other side of the coin

definitions.text: the other side of the coin

blocks.note: first meaning: the face of a coin bearing the head

blocks.clueFragment: the other side of the coin
blocks.note: second meaning, the idiom: the counterpart or opposite of a fact

explanation.surface: Toss a coin and, if heads lands upwards, look at the flip side too.
explanation.walkthrough: The obverse is the heads side, so it is ironic that the word also means 'the other side of the coin' in the figurative sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Numismatists call the principal face of a coin its obverse; figuratively the word means a counterpart or complementary aspect.

clue.text: Large fruit in US city

explanation.surface: Outsized fruit is on sale in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Apple is the well-known nickname for New York City.

clue.text: Morning after Scotland reveals swindle

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other in the answer

blocks.note: SC is an abbreviation for Scotland

explanation.surface: The morning after a Scotland match uncovers a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a dishonest scheme to cheat people out of money, the same as a swindle.

clue.text: Fancy Google having unknown earth science!

indicators.note: fancy as a verb or adjective suggests something elaborated or invented, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Imagine the search engine not knowing anything about earth science!
explanation.definitionFit: Geology is the study of rocks, the planet's structure and its history, an earth science.

clue.text: Beetle for female feathered friend

explanation.surface: A beetle is offered to a hen bird as food.
explanation.walkthrough: LADYBIRD is the British name for the insect Americans call a ladybug.
explanation.definitionFit: The ladybird is a small round red beetle with black spots.

clue.text: Arsenic's not rare, in the normal course of events

definitions.text: in the normal course of events

blocks.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
something usual is common, not rare

explanation.surface: Poisoning with arsenic is commonplace, as things normally go.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the customary way, as things generally happen.

clue.text: Chief gets in breakfast foods for intellectuals

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so one piece goes inside the other

explanation.surface: The boss sneaks into the breakfast meal that brainy people eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets in' could be read as arriving; here it means one word is placed inside the other, splitting it in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Egghead is an informal, often mocking term for a highly academic or bookish person.

clue.text: He initially rushed over into conflagration, showing courage

indicators.note: initially points to the start of each of the following words, so their first letters are taken

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A man dashed bravely into a blazing fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' seems to apply to 'He', but it acts on the four words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroic describes the bold, daring behaviour of a hero, which shows courage.

clue.text: Corporal running by lido

indicators.note: things running about are in motion and out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An army corporal jogs past the open-air swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporal' looks like the army rank; here it is the adjective meaning of the body. A lido is a public outdoor pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporal as an adjective means relating to the body, as in corporal punishment.

clue.text: Each following insect's calling system

indicators.note: following places one piece behind the other in the answer

blocks.note: per means each, as in a pound per person

explanation.surface: Every insect behind another communicates by its own signalling method.
explanation.definitionFit: A beeper is a pager, a small device that summons its wearer by emitting a bleep.

clue.text: To avoid detection, keep out of sight

blocks.note: first meaning: to avoid being found

explanation.surface: Advice for a fugitive: stay hidden so nobody spots you.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie low is to remain hidden or quiet, staying unnoticed until danger passes.

clue.text: One section was isolated

explanation.surface: A single segment was cut off from the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Apart means separated by distance, standing alone, as an isolated thing does.

clue.text: Gathered to make male's beds

indicators.note: to make is to build or form something new, so these letters are formed into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written, dropping the apostrophe

explanation.surface: People came together to tidy a man's beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' reads as making beds, but it is the signal to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Assembled means came together as a group, a synonym for congregated or collected.

clue.text: Scheme embraces one that's patently obvious

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A plot takes in a single detail that is glaringly evident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scheme' looks like the definition but is wordplay; the definition is at the other end.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain means clear and easy to see or understand, as in plain as day.

clue.text: Same groom changed in recreation facility

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the order of these letters is altered

explanation.surface: The very same bridegroom has changed his clothes in the leisure centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A games room is a room set aside for playing pool, table tennis and similar pastimes.
